comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
We have a script backup.sh which synchronize data periodically:

**backup.sh**

`#!/bin/sh
# Script to synchronize data periodically

while true; do
    echo "Synchronize data from /var/lib/weaviate to /mnt/weaviate_data"
    rsync -av --delete /var/lib/weaviate/ /mnt/weaviate_data/
    sleep 300 # backup every 5 minutes
done`

**And the entrypoint.sh for docker image:**

`#!/bin/sh
# Restore saved data at startup
if [ -d "/mnt/weaviate_data" ] && [ "$(ls -A /mnt/weaviate_data)" ]; then
    echo "Restoring data from /mnt/weaviate_data to /var/lib/weaviate"
    rsync -av /mnt/weaviate_data/ /var/lib/weaviate/
else
    echo "The /mnt/weaviate_data directory is empty or does not exist."
fi

# Function to perform final backup before shutdown
# On Azure app service SIGTERM is not triggered
shutdown_backup() {
    echo "Received SIGTERM, I perform the final backup..."
    rsync -av /var/lib/weaviate/ /mnt/weaviate_data/
    echo "Final backup complete."
    exit 0
}

# Capture the SIGTERM signal to handle shutdown
trap 'shutdown_backup' SIGTERM

# Start periodic backup in the background
./backup.sh &

# Start Weaviate
weaviate --host 0.0.0.0 --port 80 --scheme http &

# Wait for the Weaviate trial to finish
wait $!`

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
Hi team!

I believe the main root cause here is corrupted segment from filesystem (looks like mounted volumes, so not sure about the disk I/O).

PR [#88b0b8e](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/commit/88b0b8e871) — "Do not panic on corrupted segments" (2024-08):

Added empty-file guard in segment.go (returns error instead of mmapping a zero-byte file)
Stops panicking for multi-tenant shard load failures
Does NOT fix the underlying panic for non-MT non-empty corrupted files
2. PR [#6759](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/pull/6759) — "Segment file integrity: add checksum validation to LSM disk segments" (merged 2025-01-02):

Appends a CRC32 checksum to every segment file on write
On load, ValidateChecksum is called before the disk tree is ever read
If the file is corrupted (partial write), the checksum fails and newSegment returns an error — the panic path in readNode/CopyBytesFromBuffer is never reached
Enabled by default (can be disabled with PERSISTENCE_LSM_DISABLE_SEGMENTS_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION=true)

I will close this issue for now, but please, feel free to reopen it if necessary.
